work_order.confidence_rationale: I re-checked the diagnosis against this tree rather than taking either document's word for it. The two root causes hold: src/domain/opportunities.js really does carry a per-key read table (COMPONENT_RULES, :89-98) beside three hand-written write-path key lists (:189, :199, :204) and an independent money set in src/web/pages.js:685, and parseJson's fallback really does fire only for a null column, so a column holding the four characters `null` reaches record.name as null at src/data/repositories.js:585. The critic's four blocking-or-major findings also all hold, which is why this is 82 and not 88: AC-5 mandated a 200 from an endpoint that returns 201 unconditionally (src/api/routes.js:359 has no created branch), the degraded-experiments body really does drop caps and stop_rules rather than nulling them (:447-448), AC-6's assertions were vacuous, and AC-10's 40% target is arithmetically unreachable from the edit it describes. All four are corrected here. What would move the number up: the one judgement I have not resolved from evidence is the experiments degradation, where I pin today's key-absent body rather than invent a projection the experiments domain does not own — if a reviewer wants present-and-null there instead, AC-11 is the single criterion that has to change. What would move it down: the comment trim (AC-10) is editorial rather than verifiable, and the COMPONENTS-driven view iteration in src/web/pages.js is an addition the review never asked for — the review named the money set, not the label table. Nothing load-bearing is a guess.
work_order.understanding:
Issue #56 is seven findings off merged PR #43 (for #40): six the reviewer approved without blocking on, one QA found that pre-dates the PR. Three of them are one defect, the fourth is a second defect one layer down, and the remaining three describe a PR that is already merged and cannot be changed from here.

The three interlocking findings are real. src/domain/opportunities.js is supposed to be the single owner of 'which opportunity key is money and what range makes it readable', and today it is the owner of neither completely: COMPONENT_RULES (:89) holds the per-key read predicates, but the write path consults it only for the keys its own three hand-written lists happen to name, and src/web/pages.js:685 keeps a fourth copy of half the classification in a hand-rolled key set. 'One definition of valid' is true by coincidence of the current eight keys. The view change and the write-path change are one fix in one direction, not two.

The QA finding is the same family one layer down. shape() in src/data/repositories.js reads record.name before any readability check, and parseJson only substitutes its `{}` fallback for a null or undefined column — a column holding `null` parses to JSON null. That 500s both opportunity endpoints, the experiments endpoints, and the seed (which calls repositories.opportunities.get() and so throws before its own OPP_STALE_RECORD guard is reached, despite that guard having been written for exactly this case since #40). One helper beside parseJson covers all of them.

The maintenance finding — the safe-integer proof written out in full five times across two files, making one source file 47% comment-dense — is real, and the substantive ask inside it is the one-home property, not a density number. The remaining three findings are about PR #43's own body and work order. That PR is merged at f2aab6c, and the machinery that writes PR bodies and work orders lives under .github/** and .sdlc/**, which no plan may change. They are answered in out_of_scope rather than left silent.
work_order.root_cause:
Two gaps, both of the form 'the definition of a valid opportunity key is written down more than once and only one copy is load-bearing'.

(1) src/domain/opportunities.js: the read side has one per-key table (COMPONENT_RULES, :89-98) but the write side reaches it only through three hand-written key lists (:189, :199, :204), and src/web/pages.js:685 keeps an independent set of the money keys. A key added to COMPONENTS without being added to those lists is accepted on the way in and unreadable on the way out — the exact shape AC-17 of the prior PR says cannot happen — and a ninth money key would silently skip the money renderer on the page while the domain projected it as money. Nothing in the code or the tests keeps either property true.

(2) src/data/repositories.js: parseJson's `{}` fallback fires for a null or undefined column, so shape() assumes every stored record column parses to an object. A column holding `null` parses to JSON null, and shape() dereferences record.name at :585 (opportunities) and :654 (experiments) before any readability check. The read path and the seed guard therefore disagree about what 'a record this build cannot read' means: the guard is right that such a record is unreadable, but the read path crashes on it before the guard can say so.
work_order.approach:
Three changes, each fixing a named finding, plus the acceptance-layer corrections the critique forced.

A. One classification table, every key list derived from it (review findings 3 and 6) — src/domain/opportunities.js, src/web/pages.js.

Replace COMPONENT_RULES, RATIO_COMPONENTS and MONEY_COMPONENTS with a single COMPONENT_KINDS map, keyed by key in COMPONENTS order, whose values are one of 'money' (non-negative safe integer micros), 'ratio' (probability in [0,1]) or 'multiplier' (finite and non-negative, may exceed 1). Everything else derives from it:

  - the read predicate: READABLE_BY_KIND = { money: isReadableMoney, ratio: isReadableRatio, multiplier: isReadableMultiplier }, and isReadableComponent(key, value) becomes READABLE_BY_KIND[COMPONENT_KINDS[key]]?.(value) === true — same semantics as today's lookup, including 'a key with no rule is unreadable'. The three predicates are not renamed or restructured; the table that points at them changes, which is the smaller diff and keeps the existing test tables valid.
  - the write-side rejection: WRITE_REJECTION_BY_KIND = { money: {code:'OPP_BAD_MONEY', message: (v) => `must be a non-negative integer number of micros, got ${JSON.stringify(v)}`}, ratio: {code:'OPP_BAD_COMPONENT', message: () => 'must be between 0 and 1'}, multiplier: {code:'OPP_BAD_COMPONENT', message: () => 'must be non-negative'} }. These are exactly the three codes and three message strings the three hand-written loops return today, so every caller-facing string is preserved character for character.
  - the view's classification: export isMoneyComponent(key) returning COMPONENT_KINDS[key] === 'money', and delete the local MONEY_COMPONENTS set in src/web/pages.js.

validateOpportunity keeps its finite-number pre-pass (:175-180) verbatim — it is the only producer of 'must be a finite number, got null' and it is pinned by test/domain/opportunities.test.js:240 — and replaces the three loops with one pass over COMPONENTS. An unclassified key now has nowhere to hide: the pass finds no write rule and rejects. That rejection's strings are PINNED, not left to the implementer, because the module's stated discipline on this path is exact string preservation: code OPP_BAD_COMPONENT, message `has no write rule in this build — add it to COMPONENT_KINDS`, which rejected() (:233-235) emits as `${key}: has no write rule in this build — add it to COMPONENT_KINDS` with details.field set to the key. No test drives an unclassified key through the public API, because reaching one requires adding a key to COMPONENTS — the module enforces the property by construction and the test would have to mutate the thing it is guarding. The message is pinned here instead.

Export COMPONENTS (frozen) alongside isMoneyComponent. src/web/pages.js drives its component rendering off the domain's order, so a ninth key renders with its own name rather than vanishing from the page. NOTE the shape: COMPONENT_LABELS in src/web/pages.js:671 is an ARRAY OF [key, label] PAIRS, not a map, and this change inverts the iteration source — look each key up with a find over the pairs, do not index an object. A same-named object-form map exists in test/domain/opportunity-readability.test.js:37 and is a different thing.

B. The proof has one home (review finding 4) — src/domain/opportunities.js, src/api/routes.js.

Keep the full argument — a readable value_micros is a non-negative safe integer and a readable pSuccess is in [0,1], therefore trunc(value_micros x pSuccess) - cost_micros is inside the safe-integer range and IS a safe integer, therefore the guard in expectedContribution is unreachable through the wire — in the doc comment on isReadableComponent, tightened to the argument plus its two consequences. Cut the restatement from four sites and replace each with a pointer naming isReadableComponent: the module header (:23-29), the table's own doc (:78-88), the expectedContribution comment (:284-288), and the CONTRACT comment in src/api/routes.js:367-381. The CONTRACT comment keeps what a client owner needs — which three keys the formula reads, that the other five cannot move the field in either direction, that null is never 0 — and drops only the restated derivation.

There is NO comment-density target in this work order, and that is a deliberate correction. The ticket's measurable number (under 40%, from 47%) is not reachable by the edit it describes: 151 of 318 comment lines, against at most 23 lines saved if all three restatement sites collapse to one-line pointers, still lands at 40.3% — and the refactor is net-additive in comments, since the three new named tables each carry a doc comment in a file where every other declaration does. The substantive ask is the one-home property, and that is what AC-10 states and tests.

C. A record column that is not an object degrades instead of crashing (the QA finding) — src/data/repositories.js.

Add one helper beside parseJson:

  function parseRecord(text) {
    const parsed = parseJson(text, null);
    return parsed !== null && typeof parsed === 'object' && !Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : {};
  }

and use it in the opportunities (:581), experiments (:650) and decisions (:320) shape() functions in place of parseJson(row.record, {}). This is deliberately the same empty object the existing `{}` fallback already meant, so a null column's behaviour is unchanged; what changes is that `null`, an array, a bare string, a number, a boolean and unparseable text all land on that one definition instead of four different failure modes. A corrupt opportunity row then degrades exactly the way every other unreadable record already degrades: readableComponents({}) reports all eight keys present-and-null, expectedContribution reports null, name falls back to the opportunity_id, every other row still renders. It also repairs the seed: scripts/seed.js:322 stops throwing inside get(), so the guard at :332 finally runs and an operator gets OPP_STALE_RECORD naming the eight components it could not read — which is what that code has claimed to do since #40.

The decisions shape() is in scope even though no live consumer is being fixed: the proposal justified it by naming two helpers with no callers (listEvaluated/listAwaiting, :373/:378 — I confirmed they have no caller under src/ or scripts/), and that justification was incomplete. The shaped decision rows are ALSO consumed live by calibrationReport at src/api/routes.js:313 (GET /v1/calibration) and src/web/pages.js:494 (the /approvals page). I checked both: neither moves, because calibrationReport filters on record.evaluation being undefined or null, which is true for a `{}` record both before and after. But a behaviour-neutral edit justified by an incomplete caller check is exactly how a real regression slips through, so AC-12 pins both surfaces at 200 over a corrupt decisions row.

The experiments fix is in scope although the ticket names only the opportunity endpoints: the 500 there is real (src/data/repositories.js:654, GET /v1/experiments), it is the same function in the same file, and leaving a known 500 one screen over from the one being fixed would be indefensible. No page state is added for it — docs/ui.md's five states do not include one and the row degrades inside the existing ideal-state list.

One degradation is PINNED rather than changed, and it is a judgement call worth naming: a degraded experiment's body omits `caps` and `stop_rules` entirely rather than reporting them null. src/api/routes.js:447-448 reads them off row.record, and a record this build cannot read contributes undefined, which JSON.stringify drops. The opportunity projection does not behave this way because it hands the client a fixed field list and the domain makes every component present-and-null, which is why AC-1 is verifiable and the experiments path is not. The fix here deliberately does NOT extend the experiments projection: a `?? null` at those two lines would also change the body for a READABLE record that happens to have no caps, which is a wire change no requirement asks for, and the experiments domain does not own this ticket. Since the row returns 500 today, no client has ever consumed this body — absent keys are a documented new degradation, not a broken existing contract. AC-11 pins it so it cannot drift silently, and residual_risks carries it for QA and for the PR body's behaviour-changes note.

acceptance.check: A stored experiments row whose record column holds `null` returns 200 from GET /v1/experiments with its name equal to its experiment_id, the seeded experiments unchanged, and the body OMITTING both caps and stop_rules. The omission is deliberate and pinned here so it cannot drift: src/api/routes.js:447-448 reads them off a record this build cannot read, JSON.stringify drops undefined, and extending the experiments projection to present-and-null would change the body for readable records too, which no requirement asks for. The row returns 500 today, so no client has ever consumed this body. It is a wire change and belongs in the PR body's behaviour-changes note.
acceptance.how_to_verify: test: 'a corrupt experiments record returns 200 ... omits both caps and stop_rules' in test/api/opportunities.test.js; qa_script's experiments step; and it is recorded in residual_risks for QA

acceptance.check: GET /v1/calibration and /approvals both answer 200 over a corrupt decisions row, with the corrupt row contributing nothing to precision, the false-intervention denominators or the matured count, and every other decision on the page unchanged. These are the two LIVE consumers of the decisions shape() this work order edits (src/api/routes.js:313 and src/web/pages.js:494); the proposal justified that edit by naming two helpers that have no callers and missed these.
acceptance.how_to_verify: test: the calibration case in test/api/decisions.test.js; qa_script curls /v1/calibration and /approvals over a planted corrupt decisions row

qa_script: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && node --test — the 271 existing tests pass plus the new ones; nothing is skipped. This is the step most likely to catch a mistake, because the wrong 200/201 or a restated message string fails here first.

rm -f /tmp/qa.db && DB_PATH=/tmp/qa.db npm run sdlc:seed, then PORT=3111 DB_PATH=/tmp/qa.db node src/index.js in the background; wait for curl -fsS http://localhost:3111/health to answer {"status":"ok"}.

Write one corrupt row directly into the scratch database: INSERT OR REPLACE INTO opportunities (tenant_id, opportunity_id, record, score, created_at) VALUES ('tenant_demo','opp_qa_null','null',0.5,'2026-09-25T20:00:00.000Z'); — the record column is NOT NULL, so a null column is not reachable and QA's own repro uses this same row.

curl -i http://localhost:3111/v1/opportunities — expect 200 (not 500). In the body, opp_qa_null has all eight component keys present with null values, name equal to 'opp_qa_null', and the three seeded opportunities are byte-identical to a run without the corrupt row.

curl -i -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:3111/opportunities — expect 200. In the page, the opp_qa_null row shows the em-dash on all eight components and opp_seed_expensive still shows its rupee value and its multipliers.

Repeat the previous two steps with the record column set to '[1,2,3]', then '"just a string"', then '5', then 'true', then '{}' — expect 200 every time and the same eight-null projection, never the raw stored value. '{}' is the control: it behaved this way before the fix too.

Repeat for the experiments table with a record of 'null' at exp_qa_null: curl -i http://localhost:3111/v1/experiments — expect 200, with exp_qa_null's name equal to its id, the seeded experiments unchanged, and BOTH caps and stop_rules ABSENT from the corrupt row's object. They being absent rather than null is the pinned degradation (AC-11), not a second bug to file — but say so in the QA report, because it is a wire change a client owner needs told.

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3111/v1/opportunities -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"opportunity_id":"opp_qa_null","tenant_id":"tenant_demo","value_micros":6000000000,"pSuccess":0.6,"fit":0.9,"infoValue":1.2,"reversibility":0.9,"cost_micros":1900000000,"downside":2,"delay":1}' — expect HTTP 201 (the handler is unconditional; do NOT expect 200), created:false, and expected_contribution_micros null.

Write a corrupt decisions row (INSERT OR REPLACE with a record of 'null') and curl both http://localhost:3111/v1/calibration and http://localhost:3111/approvals — expect 200 from each, with the corrupt decision contributing nothing to precision, the false-intervention rate or the evaluated count (AC-12).

Stop the server, then overwrite opp_seed_expensive: UPDATE opportunities SET record = 'null' WHERE opportunity_id = 'opp_seed_expensive'; and run DB_PATH=/tmp/qa.db npm run sdlc:seed — expect a NON-ZERO exit whose output LEADS WITH OPP_STALE_RECORD naming the eight unreadable components, and which contains no TypeError and no 'Cannot read properties of null'. Do NOT expect the absence of a stack trace: this seed throws uncaught on purpose, so message and stack are printed by design (scripts/seed.js:333-335) and their presence is not a failure.
risks: Wire-visible, and intended: GET /v1/opportunities, GET /opportunities and GET /v1/experiments now return 200 for a row they used to 500 on, and the seed now exits non-zero for a strictly larger set of databases than before — a strictly larger set, because every unreadable record at a fixed seed id now reaches the guard that has claimed to catch it since #40. Both belong in the PR body's behaviour-changes note, which is exactly the disclosure review finding 1 says the last PR omitted. Nothing in this repository can enforce that note, so it is on the implementer.

A degraded EXPERIMENTS row omits caps and stop_rules rather than reporting them null. This is pinned, not accidental (AC-11), and it is a contract a client doing experiment.caps.max_spend_micros must be told about: today that row 500s, so no client has consumed this body, but after this change it will read 200 with those keys missing. The alternative — making the experiments projection present-and-null the way the opportunity projection is — was considered and rejected: it changes the body for readable records that legitimately have no caps, and the experiments domain does not own this ticket.

The validation range pass now iterates COMPONENTS order, so a body with two components out of range is rejected naming the earlier key (value_micros before pSuccess) where it previously named the first ratio key. Every existing message test supplies exactly one bad field, so nothing in the suite moves; the change is observable only for a doubly-invalid body, and AC-9 pins it rather than leaving it to chance. A caller outside this repository that string-matches on which field is named would see the difference.

Adding a ninth component key now requires adding it to COMPONENTS AND to COMPONENT_KINDS. Omitting the second makes the key unwritable rather than silently readable-in-one-direction-and-unreadable-in-the-other. That is the failure direction the ticket wants, and it is a new failure an author meets at the moment they add the key — which is why AC-6 pins its code and message rather than leaving them to be invented.

Exporting COMPONENTS hands out an array; it is frozen at the export so a consumer cannot reorder the wire projection from outside the module. Two callers justify it (the view and the tests) and both read it.

The comment trim deletes prose. The derivation survives in full on isReadableComponent and the other four sites point at it, but a reviewer who valued the standalone CONTRACT paragraph for a client owner reading routes.js may disagree; the work order keeps the client-facing half and cuts only the restated derivation, so the disagreement is about four sentences, not a paragraph.

The one-home test behind AC-10 fails loudly on any reword of the derivation's defining sentence. That is deliberate — the previous round's defect was a comment that drifted from the code, and a test that passes silently on a reword would not notice the drift — but a copy edit to that sentence needs the test updated in the same commit. It also has to be written against a specific chosen sentence, which is an editorial choice, not a measurement.

Driving the view's component list off COMPONENTS makes the label fallback reachable in a way it is not today. That is the point, but a future ninth key renders as `<raw-key> <value>` on the page rather than not rendering at all — a visible change a reviewer will read as a bug unless the work order says the fallback is intentional. It is: AC-8.

The experiments fix and the decisions shape() edit are scope the ticket did not name. The 500 at src/data/repositories.js:654 is real and is the same function in the same file; the decisions edit is behaviour-neutral for both its live consumers and is made safe by the shared helper. A reviewer may still prefer either split, and AC-11/AC-12 are the criteria that would move with them.

There is no .github/pull_request_template.md and no work-order generator in this repository, so the behaviour-changes disclosure above is authored by hand from this work order. The content is here; the guarantee that it reaches the PR body is not, and cannot be from a code change.

alternatives_considered.approach: The review's other option for finding 3: keep the three hand-written key lists and add a test that fails when a key in COMPONENTS appears in none of them.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It keeps three lists as the rule and makes the invariant something a future edit can forget, and it says nothing about the view's independent money set, which is the same classification restated. Deriving the write pass, the read predicate and the view's renderer from one table makes an unclassified key unwritable by construction, so the property cannot rot.

alternatives_considered.approach: For the 500, guard each `record.name` site inline (src/data/repositories.js:585 and :654) with `record?.name` or an isObject check, leaving parseJson alone.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Two sites today, and it leaves the decisions shape() handing a null to repositories.js:373 and :378, which dereference row.record.evaluation directly. One helper beside parseJson is the same number of lines, covers the seed path the ticket's own guard depends on, and gives 'a record this build cannot read' the single definition the prior PR was reaching for.

alternatives_considered.approach: Handle the corrupt record at the API boundary — catch the TypeError in the error middleware, or filter unreadable rows out of the listing before responding.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A middleware catch returns 200 while silently dropping data, and filtering hides a row an operator needs to see and delete. The record is unreadable, not absent; the honest shape for opportunities is the one every other unreadable record already gets — present, with null components and a null contribution — and that is what parseRecord produces.

alternatives_considered.approach: Extend the experiments projection so a degraded experiment reports caps and stop_rules as present-and-null, the way the opportunity projection does (the critique's first option for its finding 2).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A `?? null` at src/api/routes.js:447-448 would also change the body for a READABLE record that legitimately has no caps, which is a wire change no requirement asks for, and the experiments domain does not own this ticket. Pinning the current behaviour (AC-11) keeps a bug fix a bug fix and makes the degradation visible instead of silent; making it present-and-null is a separate decision about the experiments wire contract, filed on its own terms.

alternatives_considered.approach: Restate AC-10 as 'not more comment-dense than the next-highest source file' rather than an absolute percentage (the critique's suggested softening).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The next-highest file is src/research/sanitize.js at 36 of 119 lines, about 30%. That is a FURTHER target, not a softer one — the trim would have to remove roughly 56 comment lines to reach it, well beyond the 23 the described edit can save. A criterion the work order cannot reach is worse than no criterion, whatever number it carries.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add a test that drives an unclassified ninth key through validateOpportunity and asserts the OPP_BAD_COMPONENT rejection.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The only way to reach that path is to add a key to COMPONENTS, so the test would have to mutate the very export it is guarding, and the export is frozen. The property is enforced by construction after this change, so the useful thing to pin is the rejection's string (AC-6), which is what a caller and a future author actually sees.

alternatives_considered.approach: Leave review findings 1, 2 and 5 unaddressed, since they describe a merged PR.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The ticket asks for a decision on each. Silence leaves the next reviewer unsure whether it was considered. They are answered in out_of_scope with the reason — a merged PR body cannot be changed by a change to this repository, and the machinery that writes PR bodies and work orders is under .github/** and .sdlc/**, which no plan may touch — which a reviewer can overrule, whereas silence is not.

alternatives_considered.approach: Split this into three issues: the domain classification, the view's money set, and the repository 500.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The first two are one defect with one fix in one direction — splitting them would land a half-finished refactor with the view importing an export that does not exist yet. The 500 is a different layer and could be split, but it is three lines in the same file as the decisions shape() the classification work does not touch, and one full council for both costs more than it saves. One work order, separate acceptance criteria, and the extra scope stated in risks so the council can disagree.

assumptions: Review findings 1, 2 and 5 are correctly characterised as unfixable by a code change on this repository. Verified the two halves I could: PR #43 is merged (commit f2aab6c) so its body is history, and no plan may change .github/** or .sdlc/**.

A corrupt stored record can only be produced by direct SQL, so the regression tests may use a raw db handle. Verified: the record columns are TEXT NOT NULL and the only writer is the validating POST, which cannot emit `null`, an array, a bare string, a number or a boolean as the record.

The degradation for a non-object record should be the empty object, not a partially-projected one. There is nothing to project — a non-object has none of the eight component keys, so readableComponents returns eight nulls either way, and name falls back to the id. The empty object is what the existing `{}` fallback already meant, so a null column's behaviour is unchanged by construction.

The range pass may iterate COMPONENTS order rather than the current ratios-then-money order, because every existing message test supplies a single bad field (test/domain/opportunities.test.js:234-274) and no caller in this repository sends two invalid components.

The view should render a key the domain names even when COMPONENT_LABELS has no label for it, falling back to the key. This is a council-level call, not the ticket's: the review named the view's money set, not its label table, but the label table decides which components appear at all and has the same drift shape. If the council disagrees, the label fallback and the COMPONENTS-driven iteration are separable from the isMoneyComponent half.

A degraded experiment's absent caps and stop_rules is a defensible wire shape for this ticket. That is a judgement, stated in AC-11 and in risks, not a measurement — it is the one place in this work order where a reviewer could reasonably choose the other branch.

Pinning the derivation's one-home property with a source-reading test is idiomatic here. It has precedent (test/web/pages.test.js reads its own source and src/web/styles.css), and the alternative — asserting on a comment-line percentage — is not reachable from the described edit.
unknowns: Whether anything outside this repository consumes validateOpportunity's error messages. A downstream client matching on the message string rather than the code would be affected only by the doubly-invalid-body ordering change and by the new unclassified-key rejection, neither of which could be checked from here.

Whether the two dead decision list helpers (repositories.js:373, :378) are intended to stay. They have no caller under src/ or scripts/; this work order makes them safe against a corrupt record as a side-effect of the shared helper rather than deciding their fate.

Whether the experiments 500 should carry its own issue rather than riding here, and whether the experiments wire projection deserves the present-and-null treatment the opportunity projection has. Both are defensible; splitting them is a scope call above this stage.

Whether the pipeline's work-order and PR-body generation (review findings 1, 2, 5) has a defect worth a framework ticket. That is a .sdlc/** change and outside this ticket's reach entirely, so those files have not been read closely enough to characterise the defect — only to say it is not fixable from here.
out_of_scope: Review finding 1 (the PR body has no 'Behaviour changes' section): PR #43 is merged, and the machinery that writes a PR body is under .github/** and .sdlc/**, which no plan may change. This work order supplies the content the note would have carried — the wire-visible change is AC-1/AC-3/AC-5, the experiments degradation is AC-11, and the seed exit-code change is AC-4 — so the next PR body has something to copy rather than reconstruct.

Review finding 2 (the PR body's '## Changed' list is stale and omits two new test files): same reason, a merged PR. The cause is that the list was written by hand rather than generated from git diff --numstat, which is a framework change, not a code change.

Review finding 5 (the work order's files[] described only the newest of three commits): same reason. It is a real process defect — a reviewer scoping from files[] missed 67 changed lines — and the fix belongs with whatever generates the work order.

scripts/seed.js needs no edit. Its guard at :332 already does the right thing once repositories.opportunities.get() stops throwing; the fix is entirely on the read side, and AC-4 pins the result. NARROWING, NOT CLOSING: the guard fires only for the fixed SEED_OPPORTUNITIES ids, so a corrupt record at any other opportunity id is still silently ignored by the seed and it still exits 0. After this change the endpoints no longer 500 on such a row, so the residue is a seed that reports a clean no-op over a database holding a row it cannot read — not the endpoints' 500, but not nothing either.

No new page state for a corrupt stored row. docs/ui.md defines five states per screen and none of them is 'a corrupt stored record'; the row degrades inside the existing ideal-state list, which is the same call the wire projection already makes. Adding a sixth state would be a docs/ui.md change, which is a forbidden path.

Not renaming or restructuring the three readability predicates (isReadableMoney, isReadableRatio, isReadableMultiplier). They are correct, named well, and referenced by name in existing comments and tests; the change is which table points at them.
Not adding a present-and-null projection for the degraded experiments row — see alternatives_considered. AC-11 pins today's behaviour instead, and the wire change is disclosed in risks.
residual_risks: QA goes here first: a degraded EXPERIMENTS row answers 200 with caps and stop_rules ABSENT from the body. Step 7 of the qa_script checks it. If a client owner objects, the fix is a `?? null` at src/api/routes.js:447-448 and it is a one-line change — but it also alters the body for readable records with no caps, which is why it is not in this work order.

QA goes here second: the seed still exits 0 over a corrupt record at an id that is not one of the three fixed seed opportunities. Out of scope above, stated here so a QA run that stumbles on it files it as a new issue rather than reopening this one.

Not covered: any caller outside this repository that string-matches validateOpportunity's message, or that string-matches which field a doubly-invalid body names. Unverifiable from here, and the ordering change (AC-9) is the only thing that would move it.

Not covered, and deliberately: the comment-density number from the ticket. This work order does not assert one, because the described trim cannot reach any reasonable threshold. A reviewer who wants the number enforced needs a different, larger edit than this one — the same source-grep test as AC-10 can carry it if that edit happens.
Not covered: the two dead decision list helpers (repositories.js:373, :378). This work order makes them safe against a corrupt record; it does not decide whether they should exist.

Not machine-checked: the PR body's behaviour-changes disclosure. The content is in this work order's risks; nothing in this repository can require it to reach the PR body, and review finding 1 is exactly that disclosure being omitted once already.
work_order.debate_summary:
The critic's verdict was 'flawed' and its summary claimed the diagnosis and approach were right and the acceptance layer was wrong. I re-derived the root causes myself before accepting that, and they hold: the nine-key gap in the write path and the view's independent money set are real at the lines named, and parseJson's null-column behaviour really does produce four separate failures (both opportunity endpoints, the experiments endpoints, and the seed's uncaught TypeError). The three-part approach survives; I did not rewrite it.

What I accepted, having checked each against the code: AC-5 mandated a 200 from POST /v1/opportunities, which answers 201 unconditionally at src/api/routes.js:359 with no created branch — I confirmed the unconditional 201 myself, and the existing suite pins it. That is a criterion the work order would have shipped red on, and it is now 201 with created:false in AC-5, in the test case and in qa_script. The degraded-experiments finding is also real: :447-448 reads caps and stop_rules off the record, and a `{}` record makes both undefined, which JSON.stringify drops — so the fix produces key-omission in exactly the place the proposal argued against key-omission. I took the critic's second option and pinned the behaviour (AC-11) rather than extending the experiments projection, because a `?? null` there also changes the body for readable records with no caps and the experiments domain is not this ticket's to reshape. AC-6's assertions were vacuous as specified — typeof on a function that returns a boolean for any input, and a read predicate that is false for an unclassified key either way — so it now asserts positively, using the readable-value record that test/domain/opportunity-readability.test.js already tabulates, which fails the moment a key loses its rule. AC-10's 40% target is not reachable: 151/318 comment lines, at most 23 saved, 40.3% at best, and the refactor adds three documented tables. It is gone as a number, and the one-home property is what AC-10 now states and tests. The seed-test harness finding is right too — test/ops/seed.test.js imports `seed` and calls it in-process, and its plantRecord stringifies, so it cannot write the four characters `null`; the case is now written against that harness, and the message and code are the contract, not the absence of a stack. The three smaller findings (COMPONENT_LABELS being a pair array rather than a map, the discarded dbPath in seededRepos, and the unspecified unclassified-key message) are all correct and are now specified: the message is pinned as `${key}: has no write rule in this build — add it to COMPONENT_KINDS` with details.field, matching rejected()'s existing prefix.

What I rejected or corrected. The critic's suggested softening of AC-10 — 'not more comment-dense than the next-highest file' — is not a softening. The next-highest source file is src/research/sanitize.js at 36 of 119 lines, about 30%, so that target is further out of reach than 40%, not closer; I dropped the density criterion altogether rather than swap in a harder one dressed as a fix. On the experiments finding I disagreed with the critic's first option and took its second, for the reason above — a defect-shaped gap the fix would otherwise have half-opened, closed by pinning rather than by changing the projection. I also kept the proposal's position that no test should drive an unclassified key through validateOpportunity: reaching that path requires adding a key to the very export a frozen test would be guarding, so the useful thing to pin is the string, and I have.

Where I corrected the proposer rather than the critic: the proposal justified editing the decisions shape() by naming two helpers with no callers, and that check was incomplete — GET /v1/calibration (src/api/routes.js:313) and /approvals (src/web/pages.js:494) are the live consumers. The critic caught it, I checked it, and I agree the behaviour does not move; but the plan's reasoning was wrong where it mattered, so the files[] entry now names both and AC-12 pins them at 200. I also folded in the critic's untested edge cases that cost nothing: a JSON number and boolean (the only shapes where old and new code agree by accident), a `{}` control proving the fix touched only the crashing shapes, a corrupt row in a second tenant now that parseRecord touches three tables, and the seed's residual gap over non-seed ids, which narrows this plan rather than closing it. The critic's verdict of 'flawed' was fair about the acceptance layer and wrong about the plan needing to go back to the proposer: nothing here is a design question, so I have folded the corrections in rather than spending another council round on four sign fixes.
